name: Spiral Ride
keyCorrections: If they do not collapse: increase the rotational force — push the thigh harder and pull the shoulder harder
If they roll out of the spiral: follow and take the back
If you lose contact: re-establish the chest connection before restarting the spiral
description: Spiral Ride uses rotational pressure on the thigh and shoulder to collapse the turtle base. The spiral ride is a wrestling-origin turtle-breaking system that uses spiral rotation to destabilize the opponent's base.
shortInstruction: From the side of the turtle, place your near hand on their far thigh and your far hand on their near shoulder. Rotate your hands in opposite directions (push the thigh, pull the shoulder) to spiral them flat.
summary: The spiral ride breaks down the turtle by applying opposing rotational forces: one hand pushes the far thigh away while the other pulls the near shoulder toward you. This rotation removes the opponent's base and forces them flat on their hip or side. The spiral ride is particularly effective against opponents who are too strong or too flexible for the power half ride.
whyItWorks: Opposing rotational forces (push thigh, pull shoulder) create a spiral that the opponent cannot brace against
The spiral removes the opponent's triangular base — the tripod of both hands and knees becomes unstable
The spiral works even against stronger opponents because it uses rotational leverage rather than direct force
The spiral transition to back control is smooth because the rotation naturally exposes the back
commonMistakes: Pushing the thigh in the same direction as pulling the shoulder — they must be opposite directions
Releasing pressure after the spiral starts — maintain both contact points through the collapse
Staying too high — your chest should be connected to their back throughout
Not advancing to back control quickly enough after the collapse
coachingCues: Push the thigh, pull the shoulder
safetySummary: Do not apply aggressive rotational torque to the hip joint — the push on the thigh is a control, not a submission
If the opponent falls awkwardly, release pressure immediately and check their position
The spiral ride should be applied with controlled, steady pressure — not explosive twisting

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The spiral ride has three phases: Establish Contact → Apply Rotation → Back Take

decisionTree.action: position yourself beside the turtle (perpendicular). Place your near hand on their far thigh (palm flat, fingers pointing toward their hip). Place your far hand on their near shoulder (palm on their shoulder blade)
push the far thigh away from you while pulling the near shoulder toward you. These opposing forces create a spiral that collapses their base. Maintain chest contact on their back throughout
as they collapse to their side or hip, release the spiral grip and replace with a seatbelt. Slide your near knee into their hip line and secure back control
switch to the power half ride — the power half works when the spiral does not

moneyDetails: The spiral ride is the second component of the wrestling turtle-breaking system (paired with the power half) — having both gives you a complete toolkit
The spiral is particularly effective against flexible opponents who can sit through the power half ride
Mastering the spiral ride gives you a reliable turtle break that works at every level of grappling
fixItFast: If they do not collapse: switch to the power half ride — it uses a different leverage system
If they roll toward you: take the back immediately — the spiral exposes the back on both sides
If they sit up: drive your chest into their back and restart the spiral from the beginning
